subject: VPC connectivity: Redwood integration follow-up
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@nimbussec.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: VPC connectivity: Redwood integration follow-up

Hi Alex --

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps so your infra team can evaluate the integration approach:

Notes from call:
- Integration scope: embeddings + reranker for search relevance, structured tool-calling for order-extraction path, and realtime generation via our SDK.
- Auth: for hosted API we support API keys and IP-restricted keys; for Dedicated/Private we support mTLS and client certs + KMS-managed secrets.
- Networking ask: you indicated preference for private connectivity. Options we recommended: VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) or allowlisting static egress IPs for a NAT egress path. Need to confirm which you'd prefer.
- DNS/egress: If you use PrivateLink, DNS changes are required; if you use IP allowlist we will provide static egress IP ranges and FQDNs (redwood-inference.*) to allow.
- mTLS: available for Private deployments (we exchange client certs). Hosted API does not require mTLS but can be fronted by customer proxies.

Action items / next steps:
1) Alex: share your network diagram and point person for networking (contact + Slack/phone).
2) Redwood (me + Lauren): share VPC integration guide and a short checklist for IP allowlist vs PrivateLink.
3) Schedule a 60-min network workshop with your infra and our infra engineer to walk DNS, routes, and cert exchange.

I attached our VPC integration guide and a short checklist (redwood_vpc_integration_guide.pdf).

Proposed times for the workshop: Thu 26 Feb 09:00-10:00 PT or Mon 2 Mar 11:00-12:00 PT. If neither works, send a few times that do.

Thanks again -- happy to help with any prep items before the workshop.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
From: Alex Mercer <alex@nimbussec.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Wu <daniel@netsafe.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity: Redwood integration follow-up

Jonas -- thanks for the clear recap. Attaching our internal network diagram (nimbus_network_diagram.pdf). A few clarifying questions from our infra team:

- Can Redwood operate with PrivateLink-only (no public egress) for model inference endpoints? If yes, what DNS changes are required on our side?
- If we go the IP allowlist route, can you provide the exact static egress IP ranges and the FQDNs we should allow? Also confirm whether those IPs are shared across customers.
- For mTLS: do you require hardware-backed keys (HSM) for mutual auth or will certs signed by our CA suffice?
- Data residency: embeddings and reranker training data should remain in our VPC. For the reranker, does Redwood support running the reranker in Dedicated mode / customer VPC so that embeddings never leave the VPC?

Looping in Daniel (cc) -- he is our network lead and will own the workshop. Daniel, our preference is PrivateLink but want to confirm feasibility.

Thanks -- Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform, Nimbus Security
alex@nimbussec.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@nimbussec.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity: Redwood integration follow-up

Hi Alex / Daniel --

Thanks for the diagram, Alex. Short answers and what we can bring to the workshop:

1) PrivateLink-only: yes -- Redwood supports AWS PrivateLink for model endpoints in Hosted/Dedicated flows. In a Private deployment we can also host the control plane in your VPC. PrivateLink requires creating an interface endpoint and a small DNS override; we will provide the exact DNS records to map to our endpoint. No public egress is required if you use PrivateLink for all inference traffic.

2) IP allowlist: we can provide static egress IP ranges for our Dedicated/Private offering. For the hosted shared API, egress IPs are not guaranteed per-customer; you should use PrivateLink or a dedicated capacity contract for fixed IPs. For Dedicated/Private we provide a list of public egress IPs (we'll supply CIDRs) and the primary FQDNs: redwood-inference.us.redwoodapi.com and redwood-embeddings.us.redwoodapi.com.

3) mTLS: for Private deployment we support mutual TLS using client certs signed by your CA or by Redwood's CA. If you require HSM-backed client keys, we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key provisioning on Dedicated/Private. We will bring our infra engineer to review the cert exchange flow.

4) Reranker/data residency: we support running the reranker in Dedicated capacity inside your VPC (model pinned to your Dedicated pool) so embeddings and intermediate data never leave your environment. For hosted APIs we offer strict contracts and private clusters but Dedicated/Private is the recommended path for strict residency.

Attachments: I re-attached our integration guide (redwood_vpc_integration_guide.pdf) and added a one-page checklist. Also pasted a short checklist below for the workshop.

Workshop checklist (what we'll cover):
- Confirm preferred connectivity: PrivateLink vs IP allowlist
- DNS entries and Route 53 recommendations
- NAT/egress IPs and firewall rules
- mTLS cert exchange and KMS integration
- SDK auth model (API keys vs client certs) and token rotation
- Routing: how to route tool-calls and structured outputs to internal services (webhooks)
- Embedding storage & reranker placement options

Proposed next step: can Daniel and the Nimbus infra team do Mon 2 Mar 11:00-12:00 PT? If yes, I'll send a calendar invite and include Peter (our infra engineer).

Thanks -- Lauren Bishop
Product Lead, Integrations | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
